output.summary: The record FY2026 result is mostly a commodity price effect. Revenue rose 46.5% on flat bushels (-0.9%) and flat handling revenue. The auditor attributes the margin gain to inventory appreciation. The cooperative ranks only 8th and 10th of 23 peers, and no peer adopted a new program. The 6% cost-per-bushel gain comes from maintenance cut from $905K to $612K while the deferred backlog tripled, and the insurer found critical dust and monitoring failures at Harlan Junction. Staff do report concerns, but little changes. Drying and grading depend on a 63-year-old superintendent with no successor or procedures. The expansion proposal rests on FY2026 prices, and 2027 outlook prices are about 27% lower. Correct hazards, capture knowledge, and rebuild the case before voting.
